questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to go to Canada, because I have heard so many great things about the country. I also saw Canada as a less extreme version of the US. I only chose Western University because it was one of the few universities that did not require an english test (I wanted to avoid the test, because it costs money to take it)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It took some effort, but it was manageable

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an 'introduction week' for international- and exchange students. The first day was dedicated to getting help with general questions about the university, housing, working abroad - really just any questions you might have.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing on airbnb, but you have to be fast, because many students are looking for housing at the same time as you. I looked at many airbnb's that were suddenly booked before I could discuss it with my future roommates (two other girls from UCPH)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You miss out on a lot of the social events and just the student community in general. Also, it is not fun to have to take public transport to campus. I lived 30-40 minutes away from campus, and the buses were extremely unreliable. It didn't help that there was so much construction going on around town that most bus routes had been temporarily changed (which did not show up on google maps). So it took about a month to become familiar with the bus routes - and even then, they were always either early or late (mostly late though). I have sometimes waited up to 45 minutes  for a bus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't live in student housing

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was relatively easy

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You went to a website where you could browse through the courses available. As an exchange student, you are only allowed courses on the main campus. You had to select your chosen courses on another website, and then you had to wait for them to be approved. Once they were approved, the employees at the abroad department would enroll you in the approved courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always email the abroad department with any questions. They are very friendly and quick to reply.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure that there are several courses that you might want to have, just in case you don't get the courses you first apply for. I have friends who didn't get the courses they wanted and then had to take other courses that they were completely uninterested in.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't like the testing. They had a lot of multiple choice exams, and many of the in-person written exams were written by hand.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the courses and the academic level is lower at Western than at UCPH. Even the second-year course I took felt like Danish gymnasium. One of our assignments in my American Nightmare course (Introduction to American studies - a second year course) was "prepare a presentation to a ninth grade class and talk to them about wealth inequality in the US" (and then we just wrote the transcripts to the presentation).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Generally similar teaching style, but then there were often quizzes you had to do (once every other week for some courses). We were also graded for participation in two of the courses I took, so you had to be active in class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: American Nightmare; Advertising and Society; Technology and Society; Equity, Diversity, and Human Rights.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the Advertising and Society course. It was really interesting and thought provoking.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
What I reported under 'insurance' is the total I paid for both the mandatory insurance from the university AND my own personal insurance.

I only had one course book. All other courses had exclusively online material. So I only spent 150 DKK on books in total that semester.

Regarding transport, I had to pay a one-time fee for a card that would allow me to use public transportation as much as I wanted (this was done through Western, and I just used my student card as my bus card). The card was actually valid for an entire year. It was not possible to buy public transport for just one semester.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: When you get a new sim card, you can expect really high prices on data compared to Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are several clubs to join that focus on all kinds of things. There was also a street festival in the first month where everyone wore purple Western merch. For international- and exchange students, there was also a thing called "Global Café" that was held every Thursday where we would play board games, eat snacks, and get to know each other.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Be very active in the intro week, because this is where you will meet new people and make friends. Most of the people I talked to during the semester were those I met during intro week. Also, join Global Café - it is a lot of fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you have a chance, you should definitely go to Banff National Park during reading week. I went there with my friend group, and it is just such a beautiful place! You should especially go see Lake Louise.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: People are generally really nice and friendly, so it was easy to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Like I said, I didn't really talk to many local students, so I'm not the best person to ask. It is probably a good idea to join a club. I did join a club myself, but I joined it with the friends I had already made during the introduction week. Exchange students and international students had their own introduction week separate from the introduction week for the Canadian students, so I didn't really meet that many local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was nothing about the culture that I found particularly challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: This is a really small thing, but I really liked how most people said "thank you" when they got off the bus.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Stock up on any Danish snacks/food that you can't get in Canada.
2) Bring warm clothes (or buy them in Canada) - especially if you are planning to travel somewhere colder during reading week
3) Be very active in getting to know new people during that first introduction week and just generally during the first two weeks of the exchange. It gets harder to find new friends after that.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't think of anything.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know other exhange students. I had a friend group of about 8 people and we were from all across the globe, which lead to some really interesting conversations.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Living off campus - it was just annoying to take the bus every day (especially because the busses were so unreliable). It was also a little sad to miss out on the social aspect of living with many other students.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No other comments.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
